item.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
item.description:
Authors: Xiang-Yu Wu, Han Gao, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Ralf Rapp

Updated: 2026-11-25

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $ρ$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.

item.title: Equilibrium baseline for transverse-momentum correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 3$-$39$ GeV: Conservation laws, resonance decays, quantum statistics, and collective flow
item.description:
Authors: Oleh Savchuk

Updated: 2026-11-25

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Event-by-event transverse-momentum correlations measured by STAR in Au+Au collisions exhibit a nonmonotonic energy dependence with a minimum near $\sqrt{s_{NN}} \approx 5$-$8$ GeV and a steep rise toward $3$ GeV. Before interpreting these features in terms of a softened equation of state or a QCD critical point, the baseline from an equilibrated hadron resonance gas must be established. Here we compute the two-particle correlator $\langle Δp_{T,i}Δp_{T,j} \rangle$ in thermal and chemical equilibrium from $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 3$ to $39$ GeV for 0-5% and 30-40% collisions, incorporating resonance decays, Bose-Einstein statistics, Bjorken longitudinal and transverse radial flow, and global conservation of energy, baryon number, electric charge, strangeness, and transverse momentum. Imposing conservation laws via a saddle-point expansion of the microcanonical ensemble yields the variance of any additive observable as a Schur complement of grand-canonical covariances. Although the equilibrium gas undergoes the transition from baryon- to meson-dominated matter, composition fluctuations cancel the large negative "mixing" term that arises when species multiplicities are fixed event by event, leaving only a much smaller negative conservation residual. Across $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 11.5$-$39$ GeV, the equilibrium baseline with strong flow underpredicts the data by a factor of $3$-$4$ in 0-5% and $\approx 6.5$ in 30-40% collisions; at fixed-target energies ($3$-$5.2$ GeV), where the data are largest and positive, the baseline turns negative. Accounting for the data via radial-flow fluctuations at fixed energy requires $σ_β/β_s \approx 6$-$10\%$ in central and $\approx 22\%$ in 30-40% collider-energy collisions, growing faster with decreasing centrality than independent-source scaling.

item.title: Nuclear Modification of $π^0$ Production in pO and OO Collisions with ALICE
item.description:
Authors: Nicolas Strangmann

Updated: 2026-11-25

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Energy loss of high-momentum partons is one of the key signatures of the quark--gluon plasma formed in heavy-ion collisions. Through measurements of the nuclear modification factor, $R_{\rm AA}$, where a strong suppression of high-$p_{\rm T}$ particle yields is observed, parton energy loss has been confirmed in Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC. However, in small collision systems, like pp and p--Pb, energy loss has not yet been confirmed. In this contribution, a measurement of the $π^0$ $R_{\rm AA}$ in OO and pO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV and $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 9.62$ TeV, respectively, is presented. These results are based on the measured $π^0$ $p_{\rm T}$ spectra in OO, pO, and pp collisions using the ALICE electromagnetic calorimeter. The measurement of the $R_{\rm pO}$ allows for precise constraints on cold-nuclear matter effects. In combination with the $R_{\rm OO}$, this allows for a separation of cold and hot nuclear matter contributions and enables a quantitative determination of partonic energy loss in OO collisions. The measurements are compared to theoretical model calculations that include both cold and hot nuclear matter effects.

item.title: Introducing Parton-Level Fluctuations in the TRENTo-Sea Model
item.description:
Authors: Jacob Reinach, Andreas Kirchner

Updated: 2026-11-25

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

A variety of experimental and theoretical data suggest that initial condition models for heavy-ion collisions contain a degree of sub-nucleonic fluctuations. While current models fit the number and size of these fluctuations to data, we use nuclear parton distribution functions to constrain sub-nucleonic structure and fluctuations in TRENTo-Sea, an extension of TRENTo. Sampling the momentum fraction distributions of quarks and gluons in heavy ions, we use perturbative quantum chromodynamics to collide nuclei at the parton level, and we introduce an infrared center-of-momentum damping scale which is tuned to proton-proton cross sections. We find that our model successfully reproduces the $\varepsilon_2\{2\}$ of data-calibrated models except in central collisions, and an analysis of the power spectrum and granularity of the pre-equilibrium fireball shows that the number of low-$x$ partons in a nucleon has a significant effect on the local transverse geometry. Our model is largely insensitive to variations of the infrared parameters, as such changes are absorbed into the calibration of the infrared regulator. We expect that this work will aid future research on soft-hard correlations and constraining different nPDF sets.

item.title: RMT${}_2$: Random Spectral Correlations for CFT${}_2$ and AdS${}_3$ Gravity
item.description:
Authors: Jan Boruch, Gabriele Di Ubaldo, Felix M. Haehl, Eric Perlmutter, Moshe Rozali

Updated: 2026-11-24

Category: hep-th

Abstract:

We present the full framework of RMT${}_2$, a consistent unification of random matrix theory and modular invariance. The systematic prescription, which augments the existing construction by incorporating spin, lifts random matrix correlators to $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ Poincaré sums of their Mellin transforms, in a manner which enforces random matrix correlations near extremality in every spinning primary sector. The resulting RMT${}_2$ correlators are further expressible in terms of an orthogonal basis of Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms. We demonstrate the construction by lifting the two-point correlators at arbitrary genus of the Airy model, in both unitary and orthogonal symmetry classes, exhibiting the modular-invariant topological expansion of RMT${}_2$; a resummation of the genus expansion shows that the modular-invariant spectral form factor preserves the ramp-plateau structure. Holographically, RMT${}_2$ provides a concrete benchmark and explicit candidate expressions for comparison with off-shell wormhole amplitudes in AdS${}_3$ gravity, with any number of torus boundaries. We explicitly compute the universal RMT${}_2$ three-point correlator, corresponding to the putative three-boundary wormhole.

item.title: Z-Boson Production in Proton-Lead Collisions with MRW Nuclear TMDs
item.description:
Authors: S. Rezaie, K. Azizi

Updated: 2026-11-24

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

The production of dileptons in proton-lead collisions probes the transverse-momentum structure of partons in a nuclear environment. We summarize a $k_t$-factorization study of $Z$ boson production at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16\,\mathrm{TeV}$, comparing transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions constructed with leading-order and Next-to-leading-order Martin-Ryskin-Watt (LO-MRW and NLO-MRW) prescriptions. Parton-level predictions obtained with \textsc{KaTie} are confronted with the CMS measurements in two invariant-mass regions, using the dilepton transverse momentum, $φ^*_η$ and center-of-mass rapidity. The models describe the overall trends near the $Z$ resonance, while the virtuality constraint in NLO-MRW changes the high-transverse-momentum behavior. At lower dilepton masses, both prescriptions underestimate parts of the data, particularly the NLO-MRW result. These comparisons illustrate both the potential and the limitations of last-step-evolution nuclear TMD models for $Z$ boson production in proton-nucleus collisions.

item.title: Z boson production in lead-lead collisions: An investigation Utilizing MRW nuclear TMDs
item.description:
Authors: S. Rezaie, R. Kord Valeshabadi, K. Azizi

Updated: 2026-11-24

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We investigate $Z$-boson production in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$ within the $k_t$-factorization framework, using four nuclear transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution (TMD) prescriptions, namely LO-MRW, VO-MRW, MVO-MRW, and MKMRW. The aim of this study is to examine how different ordering conditions and normalization treatments influence the theoretical description of this process. We calculate the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions using the parton-level KaTie event generator and compare the predictions with CMS measurements and collinear NLO calculations. This comparison allows us to assess the sensitivity of the predicted distributions to the choice of UPDF prescription.

item.title: The impact of phase transitions on dilepton production
item.description:
Authors: Renan Góes-Hirayama, Hannah Elfner

Updated: 2026-11-24

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We calculate dielectron yields at beam energies relevant for the CBM experiment at FAIR and the STAR Beam Energy Scan. The production of intermediate mass dielectrons is expected to increase in presence of a phase transition due to the latent heat. In this work, we use the SMASH+vHLLE hybrid model to quantify this enhancement in two scenarios: with a toy equation of state consisting of the Bag Model and Hadron Resonance Gas, separated by a Maxwell-constructed transition; and with a more realistic equation of state containing a critical endpoint, based on the 3D Ising universality class. We confirm that the dilepton yield increases when the system passes through a first-order phase transition, by about 7% in the realistic scenario.

item.title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
item.description:
Authors: Kishora Nayak

Updated: 2026-11-24

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $λ_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

item.title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
item.description:
Authors: Allan E. F. G. Ferreira, Thiago S. Domingues, Matthew Luzum, Cesar A. Bernardes

Updated: 2026-11-23

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $σ_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $τ_R$ and $α$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(ζ/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

item.title: 1+1 dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration
item.description:
Authors: Shuoyan Liu, Ze-Fang Jiang

Updated: 2026-11-23

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We study $(1+1)$-dimensional relativistic viscous magnetohydrodynamics with self-consistent longitudinal acceleration under the conformal equation of state $\varepsilon=3p$. We evolve temperature, fluid rapidity, and shear stress using energy conservation, longitudinal momentum conservation, and a shear-relaxation law in a prescribed transverse magnetic stress. Moving beyond longitudinal boost invariance, we derive perturbative analytical expressions in the Navier--Stokes approximation and obtain nonlinear solutions with shear relaxation, comparing dynamical and prescribed accelerating flows from identical initial conditions. The initial temperature curvature generates a longitudinal pressure gradient that alters the rapidity slope, modifies longitudinal expansion work, and produces a distinct cooling history. For the reference parameters, shear viscosity enhances the resulting central temperature difference much more strongly than the prescribed magnetic stress, while the condition for equal central temperatures shifts with proper time and initial shear. At $χ=λ^*=0.03$, the maximum relative difference in central temperature is $0.18\%$ over $0.6$--$6$~fm/$c$, despite a persistent momentum residual in the prescribed flow. Because the velocity mapping also enters the entropy per unit fluid rapidity, the rapidity distribution remains sensitive to the flow evolution even when central temperatures closely agree. Replacing the prescribed field with ideal induction removes direct magnetic work while retaining magnetic pressure and inertia in the longitudinal momentum balance.

item.title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
item.description:
Authors: Hadi Mehrabpour, Abhisek Saha, Li Yan

Updated: 2026-11-23

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Relativistic nuclear collisions encode nuclear shape in collective flow, yet the potential of identified hadrons to disentangle deformation modes remains largely unexplored. Using event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics coupled to hadronic transport, we investigate momentum-dependent elliptic-flow decorrelations of pions, kaons, and protons in central $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions at 193 GeV and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions at 5.36 TeV. The identified species exhibit distinct momentum- and deformation-dependent responses, with nuclear-shape information persisting in their relative correlations even when individual deformation effects are weak. We introduce crossing coordinates $(P_{\rm cross},R_{\rm cross})$, defined by the intersection of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios. Variations of quadrupole deformation and triaxiality generate distinct trajectories in the crossing plane, offering complementary constraints on both nuclear-shape parameters. The corresponding behavior persists in higher-moment correlations, while an energy comparison in Ne+Ne reveals the influence of collision dynamics. Our findings establish identified-particle flow decorrelations as a complementary approach to probing and constraining intrinsic nuclear geometry.

item.title: Non-Equilibrium Steady States in Nucleosynthesis
item.description:
Authors: Zewei Xiong, Gabriel Martínez-Pinedo

Updated: 2026-11-23

Category: astro-ph.HE

Abstract:

Steady-state behavior underlies many nucleosynthesis processes in which the population number of nuclei can remain nearly constant despite the rapid nuclear reactions. While existing theoretical descriptions largely focus on established chemical equilibrium, as in nuclear statistical equilibrium (NSE) and quasi equilibrium (QSE), non-equilibrium steady states (NESSs) can form in process-specific approximations such as classical $β$-flow $r$-process. We develop a general framework for describing NESSs in nuclear reaction networks by formulating the steady-state condition as a balance of reaction flows within a reduced linear description of the relevant network subset. We apply the framework to four representative nucleosynthesis scenarios spanning different steady-state regimes: disequilibrium between nucleons and $α$ particles during $α$-rich freeze-out, the classical $β$-flow steady state, the neutrino-assisted $νr$-process, and the fission-cycling phase of the $r$-process. In particular, the fission-cycling scenario is described by a quasi-steady-state (QSS) approximation maintaining the population ratios between two nuclei while not conserving the total number of nuclei. The framework reproduces the characteristic abundance pattern for each case while providing a unified interpretation of the underlying steady-state behavior. The eigenvalue spectrum reveals network structure and characterizes the relaxation timescales of abundance distributions. These results establish a general approach for analyzing nucleosynthesis beyond the condition of chemical equilibrium and provide a foundation for extending graph-based methods to complicated nuclear reaction networks.

item.title: Sampling nucleon short-range correlations in coordinate and momentum space for Au+Au collision simulations
item.description:
Authors: Yu-Jing Huang, Qian-Ru Lin, Long-Gang Pang

Updated: 2026-11-23

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We develop a nuclear initialization scheme that jointly incorporates spatial nucleon correlations, high-momentum components, predominantly proton-neutron pair assignments, and correlated pair momenta, and implement it in the SMASH transport model. This construction enables controlled comparisons of the effects of different ingredients of short-range correlations (SRCs) on heavy-ion observables. For Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.4$ GeV, SRC initialization increases both charged-pion yields relative to a Woods-Saxon reference with Fermi momenta when the same mean-field parameters are used. The larger relative enhancement of $π^+$ production reduces the $π^-/π^+$ ratio. Controlled comparisons identify the modified single-nucleon momentum distribution as the dominant source of the enhancement, with smaller effects from the tested spatial and pair-isospin variations and enhanced production persisting without the imposed pair-momentum structure. Reaction histories link this enhancement to increased baryon-resonance production. Stronger high-momentum repulsion counteracts the SRC-induced pion enhancement by reducing the energy available in nucleon-nucleon collisions and suppressing resonance production. The similar enhancement of $K^+$ production with SRC initialization and its reduction after refitting the mean-field parameters show that the competing effects of correlated initialization and mean-field dynamics extend beyond pion production.

item.title: Few-gluon interactions in high-energy collisions
item.description:
Authors: Thomas A. Trainor

Updated: 2026-11-22

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

A conventional narrative developed for high energy heavy ion collisions prior to the RHIC program assumed hadron production dominated by hot and dense QGP formation, expansion and freezeout. Proposed diagnostics included detection of elliptic and radial flows via correlation and spectrum analysis and jet quenching in a dense medium via rescaled spectrum ratios. The validity of that narrative has come into question in recent years with detection of similar features in data from small collision systems. In response, several recent observations hint at a strongly modified narrative. Study of p-Pb spectra has revealed that the Glauber Monte Carlo estimation of A-B collision geometry is quite misleading. Collision geometry should instead be inferred by inverting ensemble-mean $\bar p_t$ data. A method has been developed to transform $v_2(p_t)$ data to quadrupole spectra $\bar ρ_2(p_t)$ that provide new insights into the true correlation mechanism. Accurate $p_t$-integrated $v_2$ vs $n_{ch}$ measurements for p-p collisions reveal a cubic trend suggesting a three-gluon interaction as the true mechanism. The p-p $v_2(n_{ch})$ trend has been generalized to describe all A-B collision systems in common in terms of an extensive measure $V_2^2 \equiv \bar ρ_0^2 v_2^2$ (number of correlated pairs). A similar program has been applied to jet-related contributions to spectra and angular correlations with a comparable result, a quadratic trend on $n_{ch}$ as expected for two-gluon interactions. Those new results suggest that the relevant data features actually represent multipole (color dipole and quadrupole) radiation from few-gluon interactions within a low-density system.

item.description:

Vujanovic, X. Wu, J. Zhang

Updated: 2026-11-20

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Bayesian analyses of jet quenching commonly constrain jet--medium interaction parameters using a fixed quark-gluon plasma (QGP) background obtained from a soft-sector calibration. This approach neglects uncertainty in the medium and prevents hard observables from providing additional constraints on its properties. We investigate these effects in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.76$ TeV using sequential Bayesian inference in a reduced three-parameter space. We vary the initial normalization and nucleon width of the medium together with the jet--medium coupling, combining JETSCAPE medium evolution with MATTER+LBT calculations of high-$p_T$ hadron and inclusive-jet suppression. We first constrain all three parameters using the hard observables alone, then incorporate a projected soft-sector posterior through sequential inference. We find that the hard observables are sensitive to the medium properties and reveal substantial correlations with the jet--medium coupling, reflecting their compensating effects on jet quenching. Propagating the soft-sector information shifts the preferred coupling relative to a fixed-medium extraction, with the update driven primarily by hadron-suppression measurements. Despite substantial differences in the medium parameters and coupling favored by hard-observable-only and sequential inference, their suppression predictions remain similar over much of the measured range. These findings highlight the difficulty of distinguishing changes in the QGP medium from changes in microscopic jet--medium interaction strength using inclusive suppression measurements alone.

item.title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
item.description:
Authors: Waqas Ahmed, George K. Leontaris

Updated: 2026-11-20

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

item.title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
item.description:
Authors: Caio V. P. de Brito, Gabriel S. Denicol

Updated: 2026-11-20

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory. Modelling the quark-gluon plasma as a classical gas of massless particles undergoing a boost-invariant longitudinal expansion, we solve the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation via a semi-analytical method based on the method of moments. We show that the energy-momentum tensor is well described by relativistic fluid dynamics even when the system is far from local equilibrium. The single-particle distribution function, on the other hand, is not well approximated by a hydrodynamic truncation, suggesting that the onset of hydrodynamic behaviour does not require thermalization. We then quantify how the departure from equilibrium affects the emission rate of thermal photons in the forward scattering approximation, and show that non-equilibrium corrections beyond the hydrodynamic limit can have a significant impact on this observable.

item.title: A relativistic von Kármán relation for assessing applicability of hydrodynamics
item.description:
Authors: Yuuka Kanakubo, Volker Koch

Updated: 2026-11-19

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is a widely used theoretical framework for simulating quark-gluon plasma (QGP) dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. One open question is how to quantitatively assess the validity of a hydrodynamic description of such a system. item.title: Isospin effects and symmetry energy in nuclear reactions

Abstract:

These studies use differential observables such as neutron/proton flows and light isobar or $π^{-}/π^{+}$ ratios. Complementary information can be obtained from neutron star observations including gravitational waves. item.title: Accelerating exact solutions of relativistic hydrodynamics and Levy-shaped freeze-out sources

item.title: Observation of Scaling of Higher-Order Flow in a Unitary Fermi Gas
item.description:

item.description:

Abstract:

The equation of state of strongly interacting matter plays a %is one of the central quantities characterizing central role in characterizing quark--gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. It has recently been recognized that the QCD speed of sound is responsible for the linear correlations between the mean transverse momentum and charged-particle multiplicity in ultra-central collisions. item.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-$Λ$ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
item.description:
Authors: ALICE Collaboration

Updated: 2026-10-26

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

The recent measurements of event-by-event correlations between the antideuteron and antiproton numbers in Pb$-$Pb collisions at the LHC deviate from the statistical hadronization model parameterizations that describe the yields and fluctuations of light-flavored hadrons. This discrepancy may stem from nucleosynthesis processes involved in the formation of composite states like antideuterons. This quantity is mostly sensitive to the quantum-number correlations induced by the hadronization process, as $Λ$ hyperons are not constituents of antideuterons. item.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of $φ$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $Λ$ elliptic flow

Abstract:

The first measurement of the elliptic-flow coefficient ($v_{2}$) of $φ$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $Λ(\overlineΛ)$ hadrons performed in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV with the ALICE detector is presented as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) in central and semi-central collisions. At low $p_{\rm T}$, a characteristic mass ordering of $v_{2}$ is observed, consistent with collective expansion of the system, in which heavier hadrons are shifted to higher $p_{\rm T}$ by a common velocity field. These results provide complementary evidence that key signatures of partonic collectivity observed in Pb$-$Pb collisions persist in light nucleus$-$nucleus systems.

item.title: Jet-like dihadron correlations in OO and Ne--Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV with ALICE
item.description:
Authors: Neelkamal Mallick, Joonsuk Bae

Updated: 2026-10-26

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Heavy-ion collisions are primarily studied to investigate the properties of hot and dense primordial nuclear matter, known as the quark--gluon plasma (QGP). However, recent observations of hydrodynamic flow--like behavior in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC suggest the possible formation of QGP droplets even in the smallest collision systems. To bridge the multiplicity gap between small and large systems and to examine the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions, light-ion collisions have been studied for the first time at the LHC. This contribution presents dihadron correlation measurements in OO and Ne--Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV recorded with ALICE to explore possible medium effects. The width of the near-side correlation peak has been studied as a function of charged-particle multiplicity at midrapidity, showing a multiplicity-dependent modification of the widths in various transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) intervals in OO and Ne--Ne collisions relative to pp and pO collisions. Further, the per-trigger normalized relative yields of near-side and away-side correlations, $I_{\rm AA}$, are measured in OO collisions for the first time, while in Ne--Ne collisions, the measurement is performed for the near side only. The observed suppression of the away-side associated yield in OO collisions relative to pp collisions is qualitatively consistent with jet--medium interactions, albeit with a weaker magnitude than in central Pb--Pb. However, the extent to which other effects, such as event-selection biases and cold-nuclear-matter effects, contribute to the observed suppression in the present kinematic regime remains an open question.

item.title: Measurement of pseudorapidity distributions from Au+Au collisions with the STAR Event Plane Detector
item.description:
Authors: The STAR Collaboration

Abstract:

To account for the detector's response to the primary particles, these measured EPD hit numbers are unfolded using response matrices determined via Monte Carlo simulations. The response matrix is calculated separately for each energy and centrality class using the UrQMD event generator embedded into the GEANT3 simulation for the STAR detector. The new STAR measurements are consistent with the previous PHOBOS results in the corresponding rapidity intervals at 19.6 and 200 GeV, while providing improved precision. In addition, the new data extend the energy coverage to 7.7--200 GeV across multiple centrality classes. This expanded dataset enables a more comprehensive test of the limiting fragmentation hypothesis from central to peripheral collisions. The measurements are also compared with theoretical model calculations, including UrQMD, HIJING, and AMPT, in order to investigate the underlying physics implications.

item.title: Muon Tridents at FASER and NA64$μ$: Motivation, Predictions, and Prospects for Precision Measurements
item.description:
Authors: Reinaldo Francener, Victor P. Goncalves, Felix Kling, Gabriel Rabelo-Soares

Updated: 2026-10-23

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

The intense flux of high-energy muons produced in the far-forward region of $pp$ collisions at the LHC provides a unique opportunity to study rare electromagnetic interactions at TeV energies. In this work, we investigate the muon trident scattering in muon-nucleus interactions at the FASER experiment, which is expected to have recorded more than $10^5$ such events. The theoretical description of the process is reviewed and improved. Predictions for the total event rates and differential distributions expected during Run~3 of the LHC are presented, taking into account realistic detector acceptance and the main background contributions. The dependence of the predictions on the treatment of the nuclear form factors and the impact of higher-order QED effects such as Coulomb corrections are investigated. Our results indicate that the muon trident process can be measured for the first time at TeV energies using FASER's spectrometer, with a projected precision on the cross-section at the percent level. We also extended our analysis to the NA64$μ$ experiment and showed that, together with FASER, these experiments can probe the energy dependence of the muon trident cross-section over a broad unexplored energy range.

item.description:
Authors: Vojtěch Macháček, for the ALICE Collaboration

Abstract:

The LHC results have demonstrated that small collision systems can exhibit collective behavior reminiscent of that~observed in heavy-ion collisions, opening a new frontier for exploring the connection between nuclear structure and collective dynamics at ultra-relativistic energies. However, the interpretation of collectivity in small collision systems is limited by understanding the proton subnucleonic structure. The ${}^{16}$O and ${}^{20}$Ne collisions delivered by the LHC offer an opportunity to study the influence of nuclear geometry on anisotropic flow in systems where the nuclear structure is well-constrained. In this proceeding, measurements of the anisotropic flow of charged particles, $v_n$, in OO and Ne-Ne collisions involving up to eight-particle correlations are presented, using the multi-particle cumulant method. Furthermore, the first reconstruction of the probability distribution function of elliptic flow $P(v_2)$, and the first measurement of the ratio $v_3\{4\}/v_3\{2\}$ in light-ion collision systems are reported. These measurements provide deeper insight into the role of nuclear geometry-driven flow in light-ion collisions.

Abstract:

The body-axis transition-kernel contours in the wave-function rotor are generally more compact along the symmetry axis, and $β_{20}$, $β_{40}$, $\langle\varepsilon_2^2\rangle$ and $\langle\varepsilon_4^2\rangle$ lie below the rigid-rotor results in a wide range of $κ$. item.title: Heavy-Quark Dynamics from $D^{0}$-Meson Anisotropy-Response Scaling Violations
item.description:

Abstract:

A species-resolved anisotropy-response scaling framework is used to investigate heavy-quark dynamics through the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) azimuthal anisotropies of $D^0$ mesons. The independently constrained light-flavor response provides a direct null test: the transformed $D^0$ harmonics exhibit approximate inter-harmonic closure but remain systematically displaced from the kaon-anchored scaling function, revealing a charm scaling violation. The common response is recovered through a charm-specific attenuation rescaling, $k_c$, together with a small low-$p_T$ hadronic-rescattering correction, $ζ_{\rm hs}\simeq0.06$, while retaining the established light-flavor prescription. In Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$~TeV, $k_c$ decreases from approximately $2.0$ in central and mid-central collisions to $1.27$ in the 30--50\% interval. For $D^0$ $v_2$, ultra-central p+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=8.16$~TeV require $k_c\simeq1.5$, whereas Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$~GeV are consistent with $k_c\simeq1$. The transition momentum exhibits a distinct system dependence: $D^0$ and light mesons show comparable $p_{T,\rm tr}\simeq4.5$--$5.0$~GeV/$c$ in Pb+Pb, consistent with the common large-system prescription also used in Au+Au, whereas p+Pb $D^0$ measurements are consistent with the lower light-meson scale of approximately $1.6$~GeV/$c$. These complementary constraints on attenuation strength and transition momentum provide a differential benchmark for heavy-quark transport and medium evolution.

item.title: Measurements of local polarization of $Λ$ hyperons with event shape engineering in Au+Au collisions at RHIC-STAR
item.description:
Authors: Taiki Kondo

Updated: 2026-10-20

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Anisotropic flow is expected to generate local vorticities along the beam direction, which in turn lead to local polarization of produced particles. Although the local polarization of hyperons has already been observed at RHIC and the LHC, its mechanism is not yet understood: model calculations indicate that the shear-induced and vorticity-induced contributions can have opposite signs and may substantially cancel, so that the resulting polarization depends sensitively on the theoretical implementation. Since both are driven by the anisotropic flow, we employ the Event Shape Engineering (ESE) method, which selects events with different flow magnitudes within a narrow centrality range, to measure the local polarization as a function of the elliptic flow at a fixed multiplicity. We report the measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_2$) and the local polarization ($P_{z,2}$) of $Λ$ and $\barΛ$ as a function of the reduced flow vector magnitude $q_2$ used for the ESE event selection, in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 19.6~{\rm GeV}$ from the STAR experiment. The $v_2$ shows a clear positive dependence on $q_2$, while $P_{z,2}$ indicates a weak positive dependence on $q_2$ and $v_2$. This is the first measurement to directly investigate the relation between anisotropic flow and local polarization, providing new insight into the origin of local polarization.

Abstract:

We present the Benchmark eA Generator for LEptoproduction (BeAGLE++), a next-generation, general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator for high-energy lepton-nucleus collisions and the successor to BeAGLE. The framework incorporates a formation-zone intranuclear cascade to describe hadronic final-state interactions (FSIs), followed by statistical de-excitation of the residual nucleus. Compared with the legacy implementation, the BeAGLE++ cascade introduces a discrete time-ordered treatment of hadronic interactions and light-cluster production during intranuclear transport. These differences provide opportunities to assess the model dependence of nuclear-breakup predictions and constrain the underlying cascade dynamics. Abstract:
